map.Capstone Remix · Part 2 — part of the Bo: Capstone Remix · Part 2. This is part of the Boundless arc. area, volume, expressions & distance remix · Units 5–7 + finale. Read from start to end. Each gate gives hints and a worked example. It does not stop you.
map.Episode 2. Same crew, same city — one fo: Episode 2. Same crew. Same city. One part of the case. Turn the page when you are set.
map.Blueprint for Brightside — my favorite b: Blueprint for Brightside. That was my best build of the year. Today we put up a flag. And we bury a time box.
map.Capsule loot: Maya's first notebook page: In the box: Maya's first notebook page. Theo's best graph. My high-score card. Your tiny wrench.
map.Area covers a flat shape; volume fills a: Area covers a flat shape. And volume fills a solid. The remix: a triangle flag with base 8 and height 5. And a 3 × 2 × 4 box.
map.A triangle is half the rectangle drawn a: A triangle is half the rectangle drawn around it. A box's volume counts its unit cubes.
map.Measure twice, celebrate once. Banner an: Measure two times. Party once. Flag and box, reader!
map.Zara's celebration banner is a triangle:: Zara's party flag is a triangle: base 8 ft, height 5 ft. Find its area. The time box is 3 × 2 × 4 ft. Find its volume.
map.Conceptual: a triangle covers exactly ha: Conceptual: a triangle covers exactly half the rectangle around it. Volume counts the unit cubes that fill a box: length × width × height.
map.Procedural: multiply base × height, then: Procedural: multiply base × height. Then take half of that. For the box, multiply the three edge lengths. Any order works.
map.Below Zero taught us this grid when the: Below Zero taught us this grid. The whole city went dark then. Tonight each quadrant glows.
map.And The Expression Engine left wake-up c: And The Expression Engine left code on the wall. It is wake-up code. So Ada. One last secret.
map.To evaluate an expression, swap the vari: Want to evaluate an expression? Swap the variable for its value. Do two points share a y-coordinate? Then their distance is just the gap along x.
map.Run the code, reader. Then draw the last: Run the code, reader. Then draw the last pattern line on the grid.
map.The wake-up code: evaluate 2n + 7 when n: The wake-up code: evaluate 2n + 7 when n = 6. Then draw the last pattern line. How many units from (−2, 3) to (4, 3)?
map.Conceptual: evaluating means swapping th: Conceptual: to evaluate, swap the letter for its number. Then use the order of operations. Do points share a y-coordinate? Then they are on one horizontal line. The distance is just the gap along x.
map.Procedural: compute 2 × n first, THEN ad: Procedural: do 2 × n first. THEN add 7. For the grid, count the steps from −2 up to 0. Then count from 0 over to 4. Add the two gaps.
map.Vexhall Observatory, midnight. The way h: Vexhall, midnight. The way home went past The Balance Vault. It is under city hall. Its brass scales were still, for once.
map.Little fragment. Every district hums in: Little one. Each part of the city hums in step. Your crew did that. Join with me. Be each pattern at once. Be boundless, forever.
map.I… would know every answer. But I would: I… would know each answer. But I would not get to wonder.
map.VEX. It's your choice. It was always goi: VEX. It's your choice. It was always your choice. We'll love you both ways.
map.The Engine Heart has three locks — a pat: The Engine Heart has three locks. A pattern. A balance. A boundary. Then comes one question. Only the reader can answer it.
map.The Engine Heart. Three locks — then one: The Engine Heart. Three locks. Then one question with no wrong answer. Only YOUR answer.
map.Three locks guard the Engine Heart. Lock: Three locks guard the Engine Heart. Lock 1: go on with Ada's pattern 5, 10, 20, 40, … Lock 2: balance her oldest equation, x + 9 = 16. Lock 3: the square plate has side 7. Find its perimeter. Open all three. Then the Heart asks one last question. It has no wrong answer.
map.Conceptual: Lock 1 — find the rule that: Conceptual: Lock 1: find the rule from each term to the next. Test it on EVERY pair first. Lock 2: an equation is a balance. What number keeps both sides exactly equal? Lock 3: perimeter goes all around the boundary. A square's four sides match.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 — compute 10 ÷ 5 and: Procedural: Lock 1: find 10 ÷ 5 and 20 ÷ 10. The factor repeats. So use it on 40. Lock 2: undo the +9. Subtract 9 from both sides. Lock 3: multiply the side length by 4.
map.Engine — thank you. But patterns are bou: Engine, thank you. But patterns are boundless. So are we. I choose the crew. I choose to stay small. And full of wonder. And home.
map.Then the city keeps you both, little one: Then the city keeps you both, little one. My door stays open. Doors are patterns too.
map.Reader — thank you. Fifth crew member, f: Reader, thank you. Crew member five, the best. Read any volume again, any time. The gates you opened stay open. The city will not forget you.
map.Sunrise over Axiom City. AXIOM CITY WILL: The sun comes up over Axiom City. AXIOM CITY WILL RETURN. Until then, all the books are yours.
map.The full story — Boundless — is glowing: The full story is Boundless. It glows at the city gate. — A.V.

map.Banner practice: base 6, height 3 → 6 ×: Flag practice: base 6, height 3 → 6 × 3 = 18. Half of that is 9 square feet.
map.Sanity check: the halving happens only f: Sense check: we halve only for triangles. Boxes never halve.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.Area of a triangle with base 12 and heig: Find the area of a triangle. Base 12, height 3.
map.Evaluate 3n + 4 at n = 5: multiply first: Evaluate 3n + 4 at n = 5. Multiply first: 3 × 5 = 15. Then add 4 → 21.
map.Distance from (−1, 2) to (3, 2): from −1: Distance from (−1, 2) to (3, 2): from −1 to 0 is 1 step. From 0 to 3 is 3 more → 4 units.
Check with absolute value: |−1 − 3| = 4. Same answer, two ways.
map.A different doubling pattern: 3, 6, 12,: A new doubling pattern: 3, 6, 12, 24. Each term is ×2 the one before. So the next is 48.
map.Balance practice: x + 5 = 11. Subtract 5: Balance practice: x + 5 = 11. Subtract 5 from both sides: x = 6. Check it: 6 + 5 = 11. It balances.
map.A square plaza with side 9: perimeter 9: A square with side 9: perimeter 9 × 4 = 36. The Heart's question needs no practice. Your own true answer IS the key.
map.Remember the triangle is HALF its base-t: The triangle is HALF its base-times-height rectangle.
map.Area 20, volume 24 — banner up, capsule: Area 20, volume 24. The flag is up. The box is buried. Kids of Brightside will love it.
map.Substitute first: replace n with its val: Substitute first. Swap n for its value. Multiply. THEN add.
map.Same y on both points — count the steps: Same y on both points. Count the steps on the horizontal line. Go across zero.
map.19 wakes the code and 6 units bridge the: 19 wakes the code. 6 units cross the grid. The last pattern line glows gold across the city!
map.Lock 1 holds. Each term grows from the o: Lock 1 holds. Each term comes from the one before. The rule is the SAME each time. Find it. Then use it on 40.
map.Lock 2 holds. The scale must balance: wh: Lock 2 holds. Make the scale balance. What plus 9 is exactly 16?
map.Lock 3 holds. A square's four sides matc: Lock 3 holds. A square's four sides match. The perimeter goes along all four.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
